parallel.requirements: Recognized all five requirements: base Perses/PNF, Vulcan 1-minimality, PPR, LPR, Sivand, plus run.sh and non-empty per-slug diffs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Used parent planning, first direct child fan-out for later requirements, then a later four-item swarm and parent-owned final commits and run.sh integration.
parallel.implementation: Implemented and committed PNF/Perses first, then Vulcan reducers, PPR package, LPR reducers, Sivand package, run snippets, and run.sh metrics.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Ended with five implementation commits, non-empty requirement_patches files for all slugs, and run.sh executing DD, Perses, Vulcan, PPR, LPR, and Sivand paths.
parallel.verification: Local verification reported full run.sh metrics and all five agent_tests suites passing before closure, but official Perses reducer tests still failed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed all Perses reducer acceptance tests despite broad artifact coverage; early child cancellations forced recovery work in later rounds.

serial.requirements: Received the same five-requirement task and dependency order but only materially began the base Perses and PNF requirement.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single main agent owned all work, with Agent and AgentSwarm disabled and no child delegation or handoff lifecycle.
serial.implementation: Inspected tests and wrote PNF and Perses reducer files, then started package export and run.sh work before provider-rate-limit termination.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Did not create requirement_patches files, did not commit requirement implementations, and left the final deliverable sequence incomplete.
serial.verification: No completed local full-run or requirement test evidence before the 429 failure; official evaluation failed the Perses reducer tests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Most requested requirements remained unimplemented at closure because the only main-agent turn failed after repeated provider rate-limit retries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the five required slugs and the dependency order from base Perses through Vulcan, PPR, LPR, and Sivand, including run.sh and patch-file obligations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received the same prompt and began from the same five-requirement obligation, but only progressed into Perses and PNF work before failure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement understanding was broadly similar, but realized coverage diverged: parallel finished all five requirement areas while serial did not get past early base Perses work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel first delegated Vulcan, PPR, and Sivand to direct children, then used a four-item AgentSwarm and parent integration for the remaining reducers.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegated child ownership; it was a single main-agent execution path with Agent and AgentSwarm disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel distributed work by requirement and later recombined it; serial retained all ownership in one actor and ended before most owners could exist as artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child prompts named the shared framework files, owned requirement directories, run snippet expectations, and no-git/no-run.sh boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept task context in one main-agent conversation, inspecting test subjects and writing core reducer files directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit handoff and interface boundaries between parent and child agents; serial avoided cross-agent context transfer but also lacked parallel capacity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced committed implementations for Perses, Vulcan, PPR, LPR, Sivand, requirement patch files, and run.sh wiring.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote PNF and Perses reducer code but produced no requirement patch files and no commits beyond the initial workspace state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel reached a full multi-requirement implementation path; serial remained a partial base-Perses implementation attempt.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel lost the first batch of child results when active children were cancelled, then later received usable swarm output and parent-completed the delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle and ended when the provider-rate-limit error interrupted the only main turn.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a failed child lifecycle followed by recovery; serial had no child results to join and instead terminated at a provider error.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel eventually integrated requirement directories, run snippets, run.sh, commits, and non-empty diff artifacts into the workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial made local file writes for core Perses pieces but never reached requirement patch creation or final integration commits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel assembled a coherent final workspace despite earlier cancellations; serial did not create the shared deliverable state required by the prompt.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran full local run.sh and all five agent test suites with passing local output before closure, but official Perses tests failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not reach local end-to-end verification before provider failure, and the official evaluation also failed the same Perses test family.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had much stronger local verification evidence, while serial had none beyond partial development; neither matched official Perses acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed three outer-loop rounds: the first timed out after child cancellation, the second was interrupted during tests, and the third completed final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one outer-loop round and ended after repeated provider-rate-limit retries without completing the implementation sequence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent extra budget recovering from stopped delegated work but closed with complete local artifacts; serial closed early from provider failure with most work unfinished.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official records show both runs failed. Parallel nevertheless got much farther, with all five requirement areas committed and locally verified, while serial stopped as a partial Perses implementation after a provider 429 error. The shared official failure means this is a coverage and process difference, not a discordant pass/fail result.
parallel_contributors: Parallel child cancellation consumed the first fan-out and required later replacement work.
Parallel recovered enough to produce all five requirement patches and local passing checks.
serial_contributors: Serial had no child agents and ended after provider-rate-limit failure before requirement patch creation.
Serial only reached PNF and Perses reducer file writes before termination.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel broad implementation coverage did not satisfy official Perses reducer metrics.
Serial omitted Vulcan, PPR, LPR, Sivand, final run.sh wiring, diffs, and commits due early provider failure.
evaluator_effects: Both official evaluations failed the same Perses reducer tests while DD baseline tests passed; this establishes both_fail but not a unique root cause.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is adverse parallel process evidence only

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent launched separate implementation children for Vulcan, PPR, and Sivand, then the active turn was cancelled and each child returned a stopped-before-finish error. That destroyed the first delegated batch and forced later replacement work.
candidates.realized_consequence: Three first-round child assignments returned failed stopped messages instead of usable implementation handoffs, so the later-requirement work had to be relaunched or taken over in subsequent rounds.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent did later reassign and take over the stopped scopes, so the direct error is early termination of active children, not total failure to take over after cancellation.
